headings.title: SMTO-EXE-0157 — SMTO isn't sure whether the desktop action happened

html:
SMTO-EXE-0157 — SMTO isn't sure whether the desktop action happened

GUID: eca2a497-7e51-5804-bf11-f6a2bac8ff24
Slug: ui-operation-outcome-unknown
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • SMTO started a click, typing or other change in an app on the Gateway's computer, but lost track before it could confirm the result. The change may have happened, partly happened, or may still be in progress.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the app on the Gateway's computer, or ask SMTO to look at the screen without changing anything, and check whether the click, text or setting is already there. The action may have reached the app even though SMTO never got a confirmation.
  2. If the change is there, tell SMTO in the conversation that it already happened so it carries on from that point. Repeating it could, for example, send a message twice or type the same text twice.
  3. Only if the change is clearly missing, ask SMTO to do it once more, and approve it if SMTO asks. SMTO never repeats an uncertain action by itself, so the decision is yours.
  4. If the step involves a password or other hidden field, type it into the app yourself. SMTO is not allowed to read or fill in hidden fields, so it can't check them for you.

What success looks like

  • You've confirmed the app shows the change exactly once, and the task continues from there.

If it still fails

  • If you can't tell whether the change happened, don't repeat it. Select Copy error details and send them, with a description of what the app shows, to the person who manages the Gateway's computer.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Native Desktop UI input had begun (or Gateway transport failed during a write) before timeout, cancellation or an exception, so the outcome is unknown; the Gateway input gate stays held until the native call returns.

What this means

  • Native mutation had started before timeout, cancellation or exception, or Gateway transport could not establish the mutation result. The input gate can remain owned until the actual native call returns. Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.

Why this can happen

  • Native mutation had started before timeout, cancellation or exception, or Gateway transport could not establish the mutation result. The input gate can remain owned until the actual native call returns.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect original operation ownership and current exact UI state; do not overlap another input action while the native owner remains active.

How to fix it

  • Do not replay the operation. Inspect the target with read-only ui.snapshot or ui.element on the selected Gateway and reconcile the observed state with the intended effect, waiting for ui_busy to clear; if the target is a secure field or the state cannot be verified, ask the user. Any deliberate new action must use a new execution_id.
  • Do not replay the mutation. Inspect ui.snapshot or ui.element and reconcile observed state. If the target is secure or the outcome cannot be verified, ask the user.

Retry and execution caution

  • Do not replay the mutation. Inspect ui.snapshot or ui.element and reconcile observed state. If the target is secure or the outcome cannot be verified, ask the user.

How to verify the fix

  • The original native call settles and its effect is reconciled before another mutation.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, read secure fields, record input or bypass OS permissions.

Technical notes

  • Only the existing explicit UI request may observe or mutate the selected desktop. Secure values stay redacted, stale references are not retargeted, and uncertain native input is not automatically repeated.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
